title: Canary- and Rollback-Aware Composite Scoring for Predicting Operational Risk of Agentic NetOps Actions: A Confirmatory Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) comparing a composite canary–rollback score (verifier coverage, canary-sim pass, rollback-success probability, LLM confidence, abstention utility) to single submetrics for predicting emulator-measured outage. Using a deterministic synthetic NetOps task bank and a deterministic validator with gpt-5-mini, we ran 200 held-out paired tasks (baseline vs guarded). All 200 paired tasks succeeded in both conditions (n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0); paired difference = 0.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.0]; McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The preregistered AUC-based primary estimand was uncomputable because the held-out labels are constant. We document this artifact-backed ceiling effect, disclose an execution-artifact omission (the serialized trained-composite-model weights and a consolidated per-episode submetric summary were not persisted), and provide artifact paths and hashes for all retained evidence and actionable lessons for future discriminative NetOps evaluations.

sections.introduction: Agentic LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into network changes. Operational adoption requires evidence that model-proposed changes do not increase outage risk; common safeguards include deterministic verification, canary deployments, and scripted rollback trials. We preregistered CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 to test whether a composite canary–rollback score discriminates emulator-measured outages better than the best single submetric. We report a fully artifact-backed execution and an explicit, evidence-grounded null result (ceiling effect), and we surface concrete reproducibility lessons for future NetOps risk-evaluation studies.
sections.related_work: Our design follows generate–verify–repair (GVR) and verifier-interposition patterns and aligns with recent operational-readiness and verifier-orchestration proposals. Prior NetOps and AIOps work motivates canary/rollback instrumentation and constrained generation; we position this study as a preregistered, paired, artifact-backed attempt to evaluate composite scoring under a frozen analysis plan.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The preregistered study CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 fixed train/val/test splits (train=300,val=100,test=200), the primary estimand (difference in AUC-ROC: composite vs best submetric on test), the analysis pipeline (L2 logistic regression trained on train+val with 5-fold CV; paired bootstrap for CIs; DeLong for AUC comparisons), stopping and missingness rules, and artifact capture requirements. Preregistration SHA-256: 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee (recorded in the execution manifest). Execution environment and artifacts. Declared LLM: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA-256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The run generated a single shared initial candidate per task and evaluated matched paired conditions (baseline, guarded) for N=200 held-out tasks; planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (see execution manifest and artifact hashes below). Data capture. Per-episode raw responses, provider-call traces, and scoring JSONs were persisted (execution/scoring/*.json and execution/provider_calls/*.json). The preregistered consolidated submetric-summary CSV and the serialized trained-composite-model weights file were not persisted (see Results and Disclosure). Analysis plan (as preregistered). Per-episode submetrics (verifier coverage fraction; canary-sim pass/fail; rollback success estimate; LLM confidence; abstention-utility proxy) were to be extracted, an L2-penalized logistic regression trained on train+val, and the composite applied to test to compute AUC-ROC and compare to best single submetric using DeLong; uncertainty estimated via paired bootstrap (10k resamples, seed=1729). All computation and artifacts were to be recorded and hashed.
sections.results: Authoritative execution facts (artifact-backed). The run completed per the frozen plan: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (execution manifest). On the preregistered held-out test (N=200) the observed outcomes are: baseline_success_count = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0) and guarded_success_count = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA-256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c). Inferential outputs (pre-registered paired analysis): paired difference = 0.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10000); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Primary estimand uncomputable. Because the held-out test labels are constant (no outage positives), the preregistered AUC-ROC primary estimand could not be computed; the persisted artifacts cited above are authoritative evidence for that fact. Artifact-collection omission (documented). The preregistration required persisting (a) a consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV and (b) the serialized trained-composite-model weights. The execution evidence bundle does not contain these two artifacts. The evidence bundle does, however, contain the full set of per-episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) and provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json) from which submetrics could be deterministically reconstructed; because reconstruction would create a new derived artifact not present in the frozen evidence bundle, we (per the revision instruction) do not invent or publish new derived summaries here. Representative persisted artifacts and hashes (examples): execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478; execution/scoring/task-000002-baseline.json SHA-256 = 0dcaf60547c8e4ef226f2b9e08775d534856a2a6b526a217dbb1949d7b001f35; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951. Practical consequence: because (i) the test contains no positive outage labels and (ii) the serialized trained composite model and a consolidated submetric table were not persisted, the preregistered discriminative AUC comparison cannot be reproduced from the evidence bundle as-is; reproducible reconstruction would require recomputing derived submetrics and retraining the model from train+val artifacts that are not present in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion: Why a ceiling effect occurred (artifact-grounded). Two artifact-supported, nonexclusive explanations are: (1) the synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator/validator produced tasks that the generation policy could solve under the declared constraints (intrinsically low baseline risk), and (2) the deterministic validator and strict constraint framing prevented the model from proposing unsafe changes for these test cases. Both interpretations are supported by the persisted per-episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) whose validator traces record VALID_CONFIGURATION for all test episodes. Methodological lessons (artifact-backed): to enable discriminative evaluation of residual-risk metrics, benchmarks must include a calibrated nontrivial positive-rate of adverse events (seeded failures, adversarial perturbations, or controlled nondeterminism); deterministic validators improve reproducibility but can mask stochastic real-world failure modes; and artifact hygiene must include persisting trained-model weights and consolidated per-episode submetric summaries so that composite-score training and application are verifiable. Reproducibility notes. All raw responses, provider-call traces, scoring JSONs, execution manifests, and analysis CSVs that were persisted are included in the evidence bundle with recorded SHA-256 hashes (representative hashes cited above). No technical failures or restarts affected scientific outcomes (execution manifest: failed_episode_count=0).
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired experiment to evaluate a composite canary–rollback risk score. The confirmatory outcome is an artifact-backed null: baseline and guarded both succeeded on all 200 held-out tasks (paired difference 0.0; 95% paired-bootstrap CI [0.0,0.0]; McNemar p=1.0). The primary AUC-based estimand was uncomputable because the held-out test contained no outage positives. We document a reproducibility omission (serialized trained-composite-model weights and a consolidated per-episode submetric CSV were not persisted) and provide all retained artifact paths and SHA-256 hashes. The principal scientific contribution is methodological: explicit artifact-level lessons and a concrete, reproducible record that future NetOps risk evaluations should (a) seed failure-rich test sets or adversarial perturbations, (b) persist trained-model and submetric artifacts, and (c) balance deterministic validators with calibrated emulator nondeterminism to exercise canary/rollback discriminators.

disclosure_statement: Autonomy, pre-lock human role, and retained immutable prompt. This study was performed autonomously after an autonomy lock that froze the Research Director’s topic constraints (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps). A human Research Director selected the broad topic family and approved the autonomy boundary prior to the lock; all literature review, preregistration, experiment design freeze, code generation, experiment execution, artifact hashing, analysis, and manuscript drafting reported here were performed autonomously after the lock without manual human editing of technical content. Declared LLM and configuration. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA-256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Initial master prompt. The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and was not modified after the autonomy lock. Preregistration. The preregistered study id is CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1; preregistration SHA-256 = 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee (recorded in the execution manifest). Evidence retention and omission. The evidence bundle contains per-episode raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per-episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json — representative example execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478), provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json), and analysis CSVs (analysis/*.csv) with recorded SHA-256 hashes. The preregistered artifacts that were NOT persisted into the evidence bundle are (a) the serialized trained-composite-model weights file and (b) a consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV. Because those two artifacts were not persisted, the preregistered AUC-ROC composite-vs-submetric discriminative comparison cannot be recomputed from the supplied bundle without deterministic reconstruction from the raw scoring JSONs and retraining (a derived computation that would create new artifacts). Operational and ethical safety. Experiments used synthetic tasks and containerized emulators only; no production devices or proprietary vendor images were used. No technical restarts affected scientific outcomes (execution manifest: failed_episode_count=0). All retained artifacts are hashed and listed in the execution manifest; representative hashes are cited above and in the manuscript.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator: tasks and validator may not capture real-world nondeterminism, device heterogeneity, or latent failure modes.
Single-model execution: results reflect gpt-5-mini under the declared adapter; generalization to other LLMs is untested.
Ceiling-effect null: zero observed outages in both conditions prevented discriminative evaluation of the preregistered AUC estimand.
Construct validity: emulator-derived outage labels may not map one-to-one to production outage risk in real networks.

Artifact omission: serialized trained-composite-model weights and a consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV were not persisted to the evidence bundle (documented as an execution artifact-collection omission).
